dropbox-blue.$description: Dropbox Blue — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

cream-paper.$description: Cream Paper — Page canvas, section backgrounds, nav bar surface — warm off-white replaces sterile SaaS white to soften the system

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Elevated card surfaces, content panels, product mockup backgrounds — the only true white, reserved for surfaces that sit on the cream canvas

warm-ink.$description: Warm Ink — Primary text, dark nav button text, heading color — warm near-black reads softer than pure ink on cream backgrounds

stone-gray.$description: Stone Gray — Secondary text, helper copy, muted icon strokes, footer metadata — warm desaturated gray that sits comfortably on cream

sand-card.$description: Sand Card — Alternate card surface, subtle elevated panel — slightly darker cream for cards that need gentle separation from canvas

magenta-accent.$description: Magenta Accent — Decorative highlight, occasional link underline, brand illustration accent — provides chromatic variety without competing with primary blue

times.$description: Times — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

atlas-grotesk-web.$description: Body copy, navigation links, UI labels, button text — Dropbox's primary interface typeface; geometric humanist sans with open apertures, optimized for dense UI reading at 14–16px

sharp-grotesk.$description: Section headings and subheadings — medium weight (500) instead of bold creates editorial restraint; the tight, slightly compressed letterforms distinguish it from generic sans headings

sharp-grotesk-23.$description: Display headings at 32px+ — regular weight (not bold) on large display type is an anti-convention choice that relies on size and letterform precision rather than weight to create impact

arial.$description: Arial — detected in extracted data but not described by AI
